trans-unit.note: @fu7mu4 It’s a mistranslation.

The currently approved translation is not correct. Please review my suggestion: "%{author} fez commit %{authoredDate}"
Since "atrás" is already included in %{authoredDate}, it is redundant to include "há", and "à" is wrong.
Example: Wrong: "à x anos atrás" Wrong: "há x anos atrás" Correct: "há x anos" Correct: "x anos atrás"
Reference: https://www.trf3.jus.br/emag/emagconecta/conexaoemag-lingua-portuguesa/ha-atras?sword_list%5B0%5D=%28-15%29.%28-4%29
El anterior comentario del traductor del portugués de Brasil explica por qué es incorrecta la traducción actual al español.

trans-unit.note: Hey @FerBle @AxelEsLa I'd like to suggest a different phrasing for the translation of this string in Spanish. When you delete a group or a project they're moved into a short of queue for an amount of time (I think it's 30 days) before they're completely deleted. What do you think about something like: "%{group_name} pasó a estar pendiente de eliminación". "Para eliminación pendiente" doesn't sound like the most natural way to express this status

@mjsibanez Thank you for bringing this up! "Eliminación pendiente" is usually used in UIs since available space is limited, but I agree that it's not the best wording. I do like your suggestion "%{group_name} pasó a estar pendiente de eliminación", which does sound more natural, so I've implemented the change.

trans-unit.note:
@gitlab: "...%{noun}..." must be known here.
Most likely, this won't work for a number of languages due to the article.
If we take Danish as an example, and we assume %{noun} to be "note" in this case, then there are (at least) two variants of %{noun}; "note" and "notat".
For "note", the DA output will be "%{verb} denne %{noun} som et udkast.", and for "notat", the output will be "%{verb} dette %{noun} som et udkast.".
So, in other words, unless translators know what "%{noun}" contains, there will be no way of knowing what the correct article is supposed to be.
Only thing to do here is to drop the article altogether:
>> "%{verb} %{noun} as a draft.".
Verb probably can be "Mark" and noun can be "Merge request" See here: https://docs.gitlab.com/ee/user/project/merge_requests/drafts.html

trans-unit.note: Could you provide an example of this string with the tags replaced by actual text? This is to make sure grammar is correct in the translation. If not, could you confirm that the interpretation below is correct? The element '%{command}' in the command named '%{type}' must specify any given component

@FerBle Here's the technical context for this validation message:
This feature allows users to define custom commands that run automatically when their development workspace starts up, expanding beyond GitLab's built-in postStart commands.
Technical components involved: -- Devfile: A YAML configuration file following the devfile.io standard that tells GitLab how to create a development workspace. As shown in this merge request, users can now add their own postStart commands to these files. -- Commands: Instructions within the devfile that tell the system what actions to perform. This merge request specifically focuses on user-defined commands that run after workspace startup. -- Command types: There are different types of commands, though this merge request has specific restrictions: -- exec commands: Execute shell commands/scripts (supported in postStart events) -- apply commands: Apply configuration files (NOT supported in postStart events per this implementation) -- Component: A required field that specifies which container/environment the command should run in (like "tooling-container" as seen in the merge request examples). This is mandatory for both exec and apply command types. -- postStart events: Commands that automatically run after a workspace container successfully starts. This merge request adds validation to ensure only exec commands are used in postStart events, and that all commands specify their target component.
When this error occurs: - The validation fails when a user creates a command in their devfile but omits the required component field. The validation checks not only for the presence of the component field, but also validates that postStart events only reference exec commands.
Some translation considerations: - %{command} will be replaced with the actual command ID (like "user-defined-command" from the merge request examples) - %{type} will be replaced with the command type ("exec" or "apply") - "component" is a technical term from the devfile specification
The message appears during workspace creation when devfile validation fails

@FerBle , here is a shorter hopefully clearer context -- this error message appears when users set up their coding workspace in GitLab's cloud environment. Users write a configuration file that includes commands to run automatically when their workspace starts (like "install dependencies" or "setup database"), but they forgot to specify where that command should run (which container or environment, like "main-container" or "tooling-container"). For translation: %{command} will show the user's command name (like "user-defined-command"), and %{type} will be either "exec" or "apply".

context-group.context: See where this string is used in code: https://gitlab-com.gitlab.io/localization/gitlab-string-search/?search=AICatalog%7CAdd+GitLab%2Dmanaged+external+agents+to+the+instance%27s+AI+Catalog%2E

trans-unit.note: @Blueberryy , thanks for suggested translation. What do you think about using the term 'установка' or 'система', over 'экземпляр'? I know MS term list has it as 'экземпляр', and our own glossary here on Crowdin also offers 'экземпляр'. However, given that the context of the message implies that 'instance' here implies a managed installation of GitLab product, referring to it as such - i.e. installation or system - seems more appropriate , than thinking of it as an instance of some object.

@Blueberryy , I think there ss a structural issue with the possessive relationship. The current 'для экземпляра ИИ-каталога' reads as 'for the instance of the AI Catalog', but the English means 'the AI Catalog belonging to the instance' (i.e., the GitLab installation's own AI Catalog). The possessive needs to be flipped: 'в ИИ-каталог установки".
Also, 'для' (for) should sound better as 'в' (into), since the action is adding agents into the catalog.
Suggested correction: Добавить внешних агентов, управляемых GitLab, в ИИ-каталог установки.
Please let me know what you think of this suggestion
@oleksandr.pysaryuk yeah good notice. You can suggest and approve your translation

Choose based on user interaction needs and tone preferences. Be consistent across similar message types.

trans-unit.resname: AICatalog|This agent uses a service account with the %{linkStart}Developer role%{linkEnd} by default, forming a %{ciStart}composite identity%{ciEnd} with the user who triggers it, so only the more restrictive role applies. The service account can also access all other projects it is a member of. Change its role from the members page.
trans-unit.source: AICatalog|This agent uses a service account with the %{linkStart}Developer role%{linkEnd} by default, forming a %{ciStart}composite identity%{ciEnd} with the user who triggers it, so only the more restrictive role applies. The service account can also access all other projects it is a member of. Change its role from the members page.
trans-unit.target: Den här agenten använder som standard ett tjänstkonto med rollen %{linkStart}Developer%{linkEnd}, som bildar en %{ciStart}sammansatt identitet%{ciEnd} med användaren som utlöser den. Därför gäller endast den mer restriktiva rollen. Tjänstkontot kan också komma åt alla andra projekt där det är medlem. Ändra dess roll på medlemssidan.

context-group.context: See where this string is used in code: https://gitlab-com.gitlab.io/localization/gitlab-string-search/?search=AICatalog%7CThis+agent+uses+a+service+account+with+the+%25%7BlinkStart%7DDeveloper+role%25%7BlinkEnd%7D+by+default%2C+forming+a+%25%7BciStart%7Dcomposite+identity%25%7BciEnd%7D+with+the+user+who+triggers+it%2C+so+only+the+more+restrictive+role+applies%2E+The+service+account+can+also+access+all+other+projects+it+is+a+member+of%2E+Change+its+role+from+the+members+page%2E&utm_source=crowdin

trans-unit.resname: AICatalog|This agent uses a service account with the %{linkStart}Developer role%{linkEnd} by default. Event-triggered runs form a %{ciStart}composite identity%{ciEnd} with the user who triggers them, so only the more restrictive role applies. Scheduled runs have no triggering user, so only the service account's role applies. The service account can also access all other projects it is a member of. Change its role from the members page.
trans-unit.source: AICatalog|This agent uses a service account with the %{linkStart}Developer role%{linkEnd} by default. Event-triggered runs form a %{ciStart}composite identity%{ciEnd} with the user who triggers them, so only the more restrictive role applies. Scheduled runs have no triggering user, so only the service account's role applies. The service account can also access all other projects it is a member of. Change its role from the members page.
trans-unit.target: Den här agenten använder som standard ett tjänstkonto med rollen %{linkStart}Developer%{linkEnd}. Händelseutlösta körningar bildar en %{ciStart}sammansatt identitet%{ciEnd} med användaren som utlöser dem. Därför gäller endast den mer restriktiva rollen. Schemalagda körningar har ingen utlösande användare, så endast tjänstkontots roll gäller. Tjänstkontot kan också komma åt alla andra projekt där det är medlem. Ändra dess roll på medlemssidan.

trans-unit.note: Not knowing the gender of %{itemType} will require some ugly constructs in German, unless we can use a workaround like "To use this %{itemType} element". Please confirm.
@daniel.sawatzky Judging from the context, it looks like %{itemType} can be either Agent or Flow, please confirm.

@daniel.sawatzky @leon.taubitz , here is some additional info about the the %{itemType} variable, that would inject "agent" or "flow" into the longer string.
You can find that text "agent" and "flow" in these strings on Crowdin:
1) AICatalog|agent == note the lowercase 'agent' in English. Direct string URL in Crowdin is https://crowdin.com/editor/gitlab-ee/16/en-de?view=comfortable#415741 2) AICatalog|flow == == note the lowercase 'flow' in English. Direct string URL in Crowdin is https://crowdin.com/editor/gitlab-ee/16/en-de?view=comfortable#415743
Why I am saying "note the lowercase agent in English": because there is also the string with uppercase -- "AICatalog|Agent": https://crowdin.com/editor/gitlab-ee/16/en-de?view=comfortable#419505 - It's a header of a form in the product UI. I just added a screenshot to this direct URL. <---
As long as those strings (1) and (2) are translated, they will be injected into the current string / longer sentence via that the %{itemType} variable dynamically.
Please let me know though, if that injection is still creating grammatical troubles for your target language, and feel free to create a localizability issue in GitLab

trans-unit.resname: APIFuzzing|To prevent a security leak, authentication info must be added as a %{ciVariablesLinkStart}CI variable%{ciVariablesLinkEnd}. A user with maintainer access rights can manage CI variables in the %{ciSettingsLinkStart}Settings%{ciSettingsLinkEnd} area. We detected that you are not a maintainer. Commit your changes and assign them to a maintainer to update the credentials before merging.
trans-unit.source: APIFuzzing|To prevent a security leak, authentication info must be added as a %{ciVariablesLinkStart}CI variable%{ciVariablesLinkEnd}. A user with maintainer access rights can manage CI variables in the %{ciSettingsLinkStart}Settings%{ciSettingsLinkEnd} area. We detected that you are not a maintainer. Commit your changes and assign them to a maintainer to update the credentials before merging.
trans-unit.target: För att förhindra en säkerhetsläcka måste autentiseringsinformation läggas till som en %{ciVariablesLinkStart}CI-variabel%{ciVariablesLinkEnd}. En användare med underhållarbehörighet kan hantera CI-variabler under %{ciSettingsLinkStart}Inställningar%{ciSettingsLinkEnd}. Vi har upptäckt att du inte är underhållare. Checka in ändringarna och tilldela dem till en underhållare för att uppdatera autentiseringsuppgifterna före sammanfogning.

trans-unit.note: @sravanelli @victoriaovando "Expires" seems related to a singular subject but here from URL the subject is plural (access tokens), we'll use simply "Expiration" here.

@WP_requests when you say "here from URL the subject is plural", are you referring to the namespace "AccessTokens|" and word tokens in it being plural? In that case, it is just a generic namespace that indicates the context of the feature, i.e. so that the string "Expires" won't be re-used in other contexts, hopefully. From the screenshots and the video in the original MR - https://gitlab.com/gitlab-org/gitlab/-/merge_requests/209573 - it seems clear that the label / string "Expires:' is used in a table, one row per token, so it is meant to imply singular in English. But I understand how in translation it may not work unless one uses the word "token", or something else is added more explicitly to an elliptical "Expires:". So the translation approach of saying "Expiration" is fine. Hope all this detail helps. Feel free to ask any follow up questions. Thanks!
@oleksandr.pysaryuk It surely helps! And I set target properly now. Thanks, as usual!

trans-unit.resname: AccessTokens|You can generate a personal access token for each application you use that needs access to the GitLab API. You can also use personal access tokens to authenticate against Git over HTTP. They are the only accepted password when you have Two-Factor Authentication (2FA) enabled.

trans-unit.resname: AdminSettings|Enabling dual-emit can significantly increase logging costs. Every dual-emitted field is written twice on each request, which roughly doubles log volume for affected fields. Use only as long as needed to validate a schema migration, then disable.
trans-unit.source: AdminSettings|Enabling dual-emit can significantly increase logging costs. Every dual-emitted field is written twice on each request, which roughly doubles log volume for affected fields. Use only as long as needed to validate a schema migration, then disable.
trans-unit.target: Aktivering av dubbelutmatning kan öka loggningskostnaderna avsevärt. Varje fält som dubbelutmatats skrivs två gånger för varje begäran, vilket ungefär fördubblar loggvolymen för de berörda fälten. Använd detta endast så länge som behövs för att validera en schemamigrering och inaktivera det sedan.

trans-unit.resname: AdminSettings|GitLab prevents namespace reclamation authentication bypass attacks by blocking JWT generation in projects that were moved or renamed to a previously existing project path. Only allow JWT generation for reclaimed project paths if you understand and accept the insider-threat risk. The restriction is enabled by default and should remain enabled on most instances.
trans-unit.source: AdminSettings|GitLab prevents namespace reclamation authentication bypass attacks by blocking JWT generation in projects that were moved or renamed to a previously existing project path. Only allow JWT generation for reclaimed project paths if you understand and accept the insider-threat risk. The restriction is enabled by default and should remain enabled on most instances.
trans-unit.target: GitLab förhindrar attacker som kringgår autentisering vid återtagande av namnområden genom att blockera JWT-generering i projekt som flyttats eller döpts om till en tidigare befintlig projektsökväg. Tillåt endast JWT-generering för återtagna projektsökvägar om du förstår och accepterar risken för insiderhot. Begränsningen är aktiverad som standard och bör förbli aktiverad i de flesta instanser.

context-group.context: See where this string is used in code: https://gitlab-com.gitlab.io/localization/gitlab-string-search/?search=AdminSettings%7CGitLab+prevents+namespace+reclamation+authentication+bypass+attacks+by+blocking+JWT+generation+in+projects+that+were+moved+or+renamed+to+a+previously+existing+project+path%2E+Only+allow+JWT+generation+for+reclaimed+project+paths+if+you+understand+and+accept+the+insider%2Dthreat+risk%2E+The+restriction+is+enabled+by+default+and+should+remain+enabled+on+most+instances%2E&utm_source=crowdin

trans-unit.note:
@gitlab: To avoid this inherently clumsy way of referring to one user by using plural form, below suggestions seem more suitable:
>> "AdminUsers|The user %{username} is about to be permanently deleted, which will also delete any linked issues, merge requests and groups. Consider using the %{strongStart}Block user%{strongEnd} function to avoid data loss. A %{strongStart}user deletion%{strongEnd} is irreversible with no possibility of data recovery." / "AdminUsers|You're about to permanently delete the user %{username}, which will also delete any linked issues, merge requests and groups. To avoid data loss, consider using the %{strongStart}Block user%{strongEnd} feature instead. A %{strongStart}user deletion%{strongEnd} is irreversible with no possibility of data recovery." / "AdminUsers|The user %{username} is about to be permanently deleted, which will also delete any linked issues, merge requests and groups. Consider using the %{strongStart}Block user%{strongEnd} function to avoid data loss. A %{strongStart}Delete user%{strongEnd} action is irreversible with no possibility of data recovery." / "AdminUsers|The user %{username} is about to be permanently deleted, which will also delete any linked issues, merge requests and groups. Consider using the %{strongStart}Block user%{strongEnd} function to avoid data loss. The %{strongStart}Delete user%{strongEnd} action is irreversible with no possibility of data recovery." / "AdminUsers|The user %{username} is about to be permanently deleted, which will also delete all issues, merge requests and groups linked to this user. Consider using the %{strongStart}Block user%{strongEnd} function to avoid data loss. The %{strongStart}Delete user%{strongEnd} action is irreversible with no possibility of data recovery.".

The currently approved translation is not correct. Please review my suggestion: "Si sta per eliminare definitivamente l'utente %{username}. Questa azione cancellerà tutti i ticket, le richieste di merge, i gruppi e i progetti a esso collegati. Per evitare la perdita di dati, prova a utilizzare la funzionalità %{strongStart}Blocca utente%{strongEnd}. Una volta %{strongStart}eliminato l'utente%{strongEnd}, non sarà possibile annullare questa operazione né recuperare i dati."

trans-unit.resname: Admin|The number of max seats in your namespace exceeds the number of seats in your subscription. On %{qrtlyDate}, quarterly reconciliation occurs and you are automatically billed a prorated amount for the overage. No action is needed from you. trans-unit.source: Admin|The number of max seats in your namespace exceeds the number of seats in your subscription. On %{qrtlyDate}, quarterly reconciliation occurs and you are automatically billed a prorated amount for the overage. No action is needed from you. If you have a credit card on file, it will be charged. Otherwise, you will receive an invoice. For more information about the timing of the invoicing process, view the documentation.
trans-unit.target: Antalet maxplatser i ditt namnområde överstiger antalet platser i ditt abonnemang. %{qrtlyDate} sker en kvartalsavstämning och du faktureras automatiskt ett proportionellt belopp för överskottet. Ingen åtgärd behövs från dig. Om du har ett kreditkort registrerat kommer det att debiteras. Annars får du en faktura. För mer information om tidpunkten för faktureringsprocessen, se dokumentationen.

trans-unit.note:
"Workplan" is a UI label is the heading for a text input field on a GitLab work item. The user types what they want done, and the workplan formats that into something a Duo agent can act on autonomously. Think of it as the space between "here's what I want" and "agent, go do it."
The term was coined by GitLab on 2026-05-05 (renamed from "Agent plan"). It's not in the docs and not an established industry term, so there's no standard translation.
This term can be translated as something that conveys "a plan structured for autonomous execution" rather than a generic work or task plan.

trans-unit.resname: AgentPlan|You are here to help refine a plan for the user from the Work Item context to a Markdown output with key information required for Agent to pick off the work. This plan is for the work item %{workItemUrl}. Use this exact work item as your context, regardless of any other panels or items visible in the UI. The template should have a Why, How, What format with key insights and list of steps. If the issue is lacking details, start by reading the comments. Then, ask clarifying questions to the users in Chat until you are confident. If there are pending questions, please preserve them inside the plan. Then, please proceed with updating the work item 'Workplan' widget with your output. You can erase everything was there before and add your new plan entirely. Don't preserve existing notes if they dont align with what you wrote. If there is enough information but the title or description is lacking, please propose to update it minimally with key insights. Try to preserve anything that is already present, just add on top and dont repeat the full plan. What is important is syncing up enough to preserve the intent and adding data where we had none before.
trans-unit.source: AgentPlan|You are here to help refine a plan for the user from the Work Item context to a Markdown output with key information required for Agent to pick off the work. This plan is for the work item %{workItemUrl}. Use this exact work item as your context, regardless of any other panels or items visible in the UI. The template should have a Why, How, What format with key insights and list of steps. If the issue is lacking details, start by reading the comments. Then, ask clarifying questions to the users in Chat until you are confident. If there are pending questions, please preserve them inside the plan. Then, please proceed with updating the work item 'Workplan' widget with your output. You can erase everything was there before and add your new plan entirely. Don't preserve existing notes if they dont align with what you wrote. If there is enough information but the title or description is lacking, please propose to update it minimally with key insights. Try to preserve anything that is already present, just add on top and dont repeat the full plan. What is important is syncing up enough to preserve the intent and adding data where we had none before.
trans-unit.target: Agentplan|Du är här för att hjälpa till att förfina en plan för användaren utifrån arbetsobjektets kontext till Markdown-format med den viktigaste informationen som krävs för att agenten ska kunna ta sig an arbetet. Den här planen gäller arbetsobjektet %{workItemUrl}. Använd exakt det här arbetsobjektet som kontext, oavsett vilka andra paneler eller objekt som visas i användargränssnittet. Mallen ska följa formatet Varför, Hur, Vad och innehålla viktiga insikter samt en lista över steg. Om ärendet saknar detaljer, börja med att läsa kommentarerna. Ställ sedan förtydligande frågor till användarna i Chat tills du känner dig säker. Om det finns obesvarade frågor ska du bevara dem i planen. Fortsätt sedan med att uppdatera widgeten "Workplan" för arbetsobjektet med ditt resultat. Du kan radera allt som fanns där tidigare och ersätta det helt med din nya plan. Behåll inte befintliga anteckningar om de inte stämmer överens med det du har skrivit. Om det finns tillräckligt med information men titeln eller beskrivningen är bristfällig, föreslå en minimal uppdatering med de viktigaste insikterna. Försök att bevara det som redan finns, lägg bara till ny information och upprepa inte hela planen. Det viktiga är att synkronisera tillräckligt för att bevara avsikten och lägga till information där sådan tidigare saknades.

trans-unit.note: @victoriaovando @sravanelli Can "ancestor" be understood as a top-level parent group?

@cecileduprekoumal In this case, "ancestor" means any group higher up in the hierarchy (parent, grandparent, etc.).
This string is the "conflictingAncestorError" message in the GitLab Duo availability admin settings UI (duo_availability_namespaces_table.vue). It appears when an admin tries to set a Duo availability override on a group, but a conflicting admin lock already exists on one of that group's ancestor groups (i.e., a parent, grandparent, or any higher-level group in the chain).

trans-unit.resname: AmazonQ|I understand that by selecting Save changes, GitLab creates a service account for Amazon Q and sends its credentials to AWS. Use of the Amazon Q Developer capabilities as part of GitLab Duo with Amazon Q is governed by the %{helpStart}AWS Customer Agreement%{helpEnd} or other written agreement between you and AWS governing your use of AWS services. Amazon Q Developer processes data across all US Regions and makes cross-region API calls when your requests require it.
trans-unit.source: AmazonQ|I understand that by selecting Save changes, GitLab creates a service account for Amazon Q and sends its credentials to AWS. Use of the Amazon Q Developer capabilities as part of GitLab Duo with Amazon Q is governed by the %{helpStart}AWS Customer Agreement%{helpEnd} or other written agreement between you and AWS governing your use of AWS services. Amazon Q Developer processes data across all US Regions and makes cross-region API calls when your requests require it.
trans-unit.target: Jag förstår att genom att välja Spara ändringar skapar GitLab ett tjänstekonto för Amazon Q och skickar dess autentiseringsuppgifter till AWS. Användningen av Amazon Q Developer-funktionerna som en del av GitLab Duo med Amazon Q regleras av %{helpStart}AWS kundavtal%{helpEnd} eller något annat skriftligt avtal mellan dig och AWS som reglerar din användning av AWS-tjänster. Amazon Q Developer behandlar data i alla regioner i USA och gör API-anrop mellan regioner när dina förfrågningar kräver det.

trans-unit.note:
I am changing this translation based on the guidelines in the Microsoft Style Guide for Ukrainian. Specifically, on page 59 the style guide is talking abut using "під час" vs. "при".
This preposition «при» in Ukrainian cannot be used in the meaning "during" and to describe the circumstances, which do not presuppose the presence of something nearby. For example, the Russian word combination «при выполнении работы» can be translated as «під час виконання роботи», «за виконання роботи», «для виконання роботи», «коли робота виконується» but not «при виконанні роботи»
See ukr-ukr-StyleGuide.pdf (Ukrainian Localization Style Guide)
Helpful resources: https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/globalization/reference/microsoft-style-guides https://docs.gitlab.com/ee/development/documentation/styleguide/word_list.html https://docs.gitlab.com/ee/development/documentation/styleguide/

trans-unit.note: Not 100% sure if "Build" is a verb or a noun here, assuming noun. Let me know if this is wrong.

@daniel.sawatzky Build is a noun here, meaning "build" as an "artifact" of code that was built.
Here is more context:
The field "Build Config Digest" refers to a digest (hash) of the build configuration that was used to generate the artifact. That digest / hash of the build configuration allows consumers of the artifact to verify that the build was performed with a specific, known configuration.
It has to do with SLSA (Supply-chain Levels for Software Artifacts) provenance attestation metadata. More info here: https://slsa.dev/
The goal of this UI text and this feature is to make attestations discoverable, so users can now view detailed attestation metadata at the project level
Here is the related MR with screenshots and other surrounding text that may suggest more context: https://gitlab.com/gitlab-org/gitlab/-/merge_requests/214851
Issue: https://gitlab.com/gitlab-org/gitlab/-/work_items/566595
Issue's parent epic: https://gitlab.com/groups/gitlab-org/-/work_items/18617

trans-unit.note:
The English word "severity" is often translated into Russian as "серьёзность". Russian example: "Уязвимости зависят от типа, серьезности и метода атаки". https://docs.github.com/ru/code-security/security-advisories/working-with-global-security-advisories-from-the-github-advisory-database/about-the-github-advisory-database English example: "Vulnerabilities vary in type, severity, and method of attack". https://docs.github.com/en/code-security/security-advisories/working-with-global-security-advisories-from-the-github-advisory-database/about-the-github-advisory-database
Use the letter Ё/ё instead of E/e in the following word: "серьёзность". Although E/e is often accepted as a replacement for Ё/ё, the official spelling uses Ё/ё.

The default value is dynamic, equal to the number of usable logical CPUs.
trans-unit.source: DastProfiles|The maximum number of concurrent browser instances to use. For instance runners on GitLab.com, we recommended a maximum of three. Private runners with more resources may benefit from a higher number, but are likely to produce little benefit after five to seven instances. The default value is dynamic, equal to the number of usable logical CPUs.
trans-unit.target: Det maximala antalet samtidiga webbläsarinstanser som ska användas. För instans-runners på GitLab.com rekommenderar vi högst tre. Privata runners med mer resurser kan ha nytta av ett högre antal, men efter fem till sju instanser ger det sannolikt liten ytterligare nytta. Standardvärdet är dynamiskt och motsvarar antalet användbara logiska processorer.

trans-unit.resname: DatabaseDiagnostics|The cluster default for statement_timeout is 0. GitLab sets its own value for each of its sessions, but any other session, for example psql, a backup or an external tool, can run a query with no limit. Set statement_timeout in postgresql.conf, or with ALTER DATABASE or ALTER ROLE.
trans-unit.source: DatabaseDiagnostics|The cluster default for statement_timeout is 0. GitLab sets its own value for each of its sessions, but any other session, for example psql, a backup or an external tool, can run a query with no limit. Set statement_timeout in postgresql.conf, or with ALTER DATABASE or ALTER ROLE.
trans-unit.target: Klusterstandarden för statement_timeout är 0. GitLab anger ett eget värde för var och en av sina sessioner, men alla andra sessioner, till exempel psql, en säkerhetskopia eller ett externt verktyg, kan köra en fråga utan begränsning. Ange statement_timeout i postgresql.conf, eller med ALTER DATABASE eller ALTER ROLE.

trans-unit.note: A screenshot of this text would be very useful, as my investigations didn't help me know if this means "to download a directory" or "a download directory"...

@SabrinaDeVellis , the screenshot in the original MR shows text "Download source code": https://gitlab.com/gitlab-org/gitlab/-/merge_requests/178909
It does not show "Download directory".
The "Download directory" will appear when a user is viewing a specific directory within a repository and allows users to download that particular directory, not the entire code. While "Download source code" is a separate option on he same UI / dropdown component that allows users to download the entire repository's source code.
So, "Download source code" and "Download directory" are two options that will show on that dropdown component [screenshot in the MR] when a user clicks "Code".
Here is how that functionality described in GitLab product documentation: https://docs.gitlab.com/ee/user/project/repository/#download-repository-source-code (note however, that GitLab docs still call those options "Source code" and "Directory", not yet "Download source code" and "Download directory")
Short answer to your question is, "Download directory" describes an option to a user "to download [a particular] directory".
@oleksandr.pysaryuk: Thank you for the explanation. I saw "Download source code" but I was not sure it was the same construction/type of option/button.

trans-unit.note: Could you clarify if this refers to features that allow previewing something (your work, for instance) or to the possibility of previewing said features? For the time being, I'm assuming the second interpretation is correct, since it makes a bit more sense given the context seen in the uploaded video, but I would need more information to make sure.

@FerBle Thanks for using the context URL and tracing it all the way to the video in the original MR!
Your second option instinct is correct.
In the string "DuoAgenticChat|Optional. Turn on preview features", "preview features" refers to features that are themselves in a preview state (i.e., beta and experimental features), not features that let you preview your work.
This is confirmed by the description that immediately follows this step title in the code (from duo_disabled_empty_state.vue): "Turn on beta and experimental features for early access to new tools and improvements."
You can also see that text at 15sec in the 30sec clip on the original MR.
The context is a step-by-step guide shown to admins when GitLab Duo is disabled. The three steps are:
1. Turn on GitLab Duo features - Enable Duo for the project or group 2. Optional. Turn on preview features - Enable beta/experimental features for early access 3. Turn on flows - Set up automated workflows and AI agents
So "preview features" == features that are in a preview/pre-release stage (beta, experimental). The word "preview" here is behaving like an adjective in English, describing the maturity level of the features.
Hope this helps!
@oleksandr.pysaryuk Thank you! I figured as much, but was still not 100% certain. Thank you for taking the time to provide all the extra context, I really appreciate it :)

trans-unit.resname: For the GitLab Team to keep your subscription data up to date, this is a reminder to report your license usage on a monthly basis, or at the cadence set in your agreement with GitLab. This allows us to simplify the billing process for overages and renewals. To report your usage data, export your license usage file and email it to %{renewal_service_email}. If you need an updated license, GitLab will send the license to the email address registered in the %{customers_dot}, and you can upload this license to your instance.
trans-unit.source: For the GitLab Team to keep your subscription data up to date, this is a reminder to report your license usage on a monthly basis, or at the cadence set in your agreement with GitLab. This allows us to simplify the billing process for overages and renewals. To report your usage data, export your license usage file and email it to %{renewal_service_email}. If you need an updated license, GitLab will send the license to the email address registered in the %{customers_dot}, and you can upload this license to your instance.
trans-unit.target: För att GitLab-teamet ska kunna hålla dina prenumerationsuppgifter uppdaterade är detta en påminnelse om att rapportera din licensanvändning varje månad, eller enligt den rapporteringsfrekvens som anges i ditt avtal med GitLab. Detta gör det möjligt för oss att förenkla faktureringsprocessen för överanvändning och förnyelser. För att rapportera dina användningsuppgifter exporterar du filen med licensanvändning och skickar den via e-post till %{renewal_service_email}. Om du behöver en uppdaterad licens skickar GitLab licensen till den e-postadress som är registrerad i %{customers_dot}, och du kan sedan ladda upp licensen till din instans.

trans-unit.note: @oleksandr.pysaryuk : When searching for context (https://gitlab.com/-/project/278964/uploads/a1f2fd42a85885e3fe96a659f00f2444/Failed.png), I found the sentence "Retry #1 scheduled in 34 seconds". The last variable in the source string is not the same and implies a construction with "ago". Could you confirm there is an error in the source string and that the variable should not be "timeago"?

@SabrinaDeVellis thanks for the great question!
The string 'Geo|%{noBoldStart}Next sync retry:%{noBoldEnd} Retry #%{retryCount} scheduled %{timeAgo}' contains a placeholder %{timeAgo} that will be replaced with a time expression.
The %{timeAgo} placeholder will automatically include either:
"in X seconds/minutes/hours" (for future times) "X seconds/minutes/hours ago" (for past times)
The preposition "in" (for future) or the word "ago" (for past) are automatically added by the system, and are not part of the string that's being translated here. This is why you see "Retry #1 scheduled in 34 seconds" in the screenshot in the original MR (https://gitlab.com/gitlab-org/gitlab/-/merge_requests/185152/), even though the string only has %{timeAgo}.
How to approach translation? PLease translate the rest of the string normally. Keep the %{timeAgo} placeholder where it makes sense in your target language. Be aware that the system will automatically add the equivalent of "in" or "ago" in the target language
If your target language requires different word order or grammar when expressing future vs. past times, please respond here with some details. Thanks so much!

trans-unit.note: @oleksandr.pysaryuk I don't quite understand what is meant by this. What is missing and what is "Primary" referring to? The MR does not really provide further explanation.

@daniel.sawatzky Let me give you the fullest context. Hope this helps!
In the context of GitLab Geo replication, "Geo|Missing on Primary!" means that a resource (like a project repository, file, or other replicable object) exists on the secondary Geo site but cannot be found on the primary site.
Here is some documentation on that: https://docs.gitlab.com/administration/geo/replication/multiple_servers/
This is a specific replication status that's displayed in the GitLab UI to indicate a data inconsistency between sites.
This situation can occur when:
- Some object was deleted from the primary site but the deletion hasn't been synchronized to the secondary yet - There was some synchronization issue that created inconsistency between sites - Some data was manually added to the secondary but doesn't exist on the primary
The message is a technical status message that should be preserved with its exclamation mark to indicate the importance of this state, as it represents a data inconsistency that might require administrator attention.
@oleksandr.pysaryuk Great, thank you so much for the details. Adjusted accordingly.

@nicklcanada (& @gitlab): Thx a lot for the info—highly informative as always. :-)
You might very well be right, but I don't know gitlab well enough to assess this accurately.
Besides, the primary purpose of the CONTEXT section/field is to assist/help translators understand the exact meaning of the source text, and to do so without being forced to pursue resources/info elsewhere.
So when a project owner chooses to not provide info relevant to the localization task at hand, he either hasn't fully grasped the concept of this platform, or he just doesn't care about the quality of the localization work being performed. In both cases (and the latter one in particular), it's just utterly pointless to use this platform.
The exact content of this variable is required for a proper localization output.
@NCAA You are welcome! Have a nice weekend!

@oleksandr.pysaryuk @victoriaovando this is a DNT, please add it to the termbase if possibile
@WP_requests will check and add it. Thanks for flagging. @KaterinaGasova FYI

@WP_requests The correct term is "GitLab Du with Amazon Q" without the word Chat in it. And preposition "with" is translatable. In this case , the word Chat is probably added by mistake, and the English source may need to be updated. Please translate "GitLab Duo Chat with Amazon Q" similarly to as if it was "GitLab Duo with Amazon Q", i.e please translate the preposition, but not the word Chat. Learn more here about the correct names of features: https://docs.gitlab.com/user/duo_amazon_q/ cc @victoriaovando @KaterinaGasova
@oleksandr.pysaryuk perfect! Thanks and updated!

trans-unit.resname: GitLabPages|When using Pages under the general domain of a GitLab instance (%{pages_host}), you cannot use HTTPS with subdomains of subdomains. If your namespace or groupname contains a dot, it does not work. This is a limitation of the HTTP Over TLS protocol. HTTP pages work if you don't redirect HTTP to HTTPS. %{docs_link_start}Learn more.%{link_end}
trans-unit.source: GitLabPages|When using Pages under the general domain of a GitLab instance (%{pages_host}), you cannot use HTTPS with subdomains of subdomains. If your namespace or groupname contains a dot, it does not work. This is a limitation of the HTTP Over TLS protocol. HTTP pages work if you don't redirect HTTP to HTTPS. %{docs_link_start}Learn more.%{link_end}
trans-unit.target: När du använder Pages under den allmänna domänen för en GitLab-instans (%{pages_host}) kan du inte använda HTTPS med underdomäner till underdomäner. Om ditt namnrymds- eller gruppnamn innehåller en punkt fungerar det inte. Detta är en begränsning i HTTP over TLS-protokollet. HTTP-sidor fungerar om du inte omdirigerar HTTP till HTTPS. %{docs_link_start}Läs mer.%{link_end}

context-group.context: See where this string is used in code: https://gitlab-com.gitlab.io/localization/gitlab-string-search/?search=GitLabPages%7CWhen+using+Pages+under+the+general+domain+of+a+GitLab+instance+%28%25%7Bpages_host%7D%29%2C+you+cannot+use+HTTPS+with+subdomains+of+subdomains%2E+If+your+namespace+or+groupname+contains+a+dot%2C+it+does+not+work%2E+This+is+a+limitation+of+the+HTTP+Over+TLS+protocol%2E+HTTP+pages+work+if+you+don%27t+redirect+HTTP+to+HTTPS%2E+%25%7Bdocs_link_start%7DLearn+more%2E%25%7Blink_end%7D

trans-unit.note:
Recently, I started to suggest a new zh_TW translations for "XXX Bar". That is, "XXX條". For example:
* Sidebar: 側邊條 * Navigation Bar: 導航條 * Toolbar: 工具條 * Menu Bar: 選單條 * ...etc
The main point is that we shouldn't judge whether to translate "Bar" into "欄" or "列" by observing its direction.
In fact, some of "XXX Bar" are already translated in this form. For example:
* Scroll Bar: 捲動條 * Progress Bar: 進度條
Hope zh_TW translators here can take my advices.

trans-unit.note: Is '{cloudId}' okay ? It should be '%{cloudId}' ?

@fu7mu4, thanks for flagging this. The `{cloudId}` is intentional. It is part of the Atlassian API URL format, shown to users as a literal template they fill in with their own Atlassian Cloud ID. It is not a GitLab string interpolation variable. GitLab uses `%{...}` for those, which is why `%{linkStart}` and `%{linkEnd}` in the same string look different. Leave `{cloudId}` untranslated and as-is in the URL.

trans-unit.source: Job|ID token issuance is disabled in CI because this project's path was previously used by a different project. To restore ID tokens, set `ci_id_token_sub_claim_components` to start with `project_id` (for example, `["project_id", "ref_type", "ref"]`) and update your cloud trust policy to match.
trans-unit.target: Utfärdande av ID-token är inaktiverat i CI eftersom projektets sökväg tidigare användes av ett annat projekt. Återställ ID-token genom att ange att `ci_id_token_sub_claim_components` börjar med `project_id` (till exempel, `["project_id", "ref_type", "ref"]`) och uppdatera molnets förtroendepolicy så att den matchar.

So I think it would be best if we could avoid this particular term in general.
I agree. I replaced "Programmation" by "Planification".

trans-unit.note: Context: https://gitlab.com/gitlab-org/gitlab/uploads/c02b9a57c2f4d7d3a72431e263397392/image.png
'we received the email we sent to your email inbox' ???
@NCAA I guess it should be: We could not verify that the email we sent to your Service Desk inbox was delivered.

@xdelatour (+ @gitlab): Yeah, if the pesky active voice form is to be used. :-/
Personally, I'd go with something like:
>> "Notify|Couldn't verify that the email sent by our system was delivered to your Service Desk inbox.".
As I've pointed out in many other projects, "we" should not be used in general UI texts and error messages unless to indicate the participation of staff, etc., i.e., to indicate that a human is/was actively involved in a given process. Texts are (typically) perceived and interpreted differently in software environments (UI texts) compared to hardcopy texts, which is something all the active voice aficionados completely overlook (or choose to ignore) when they praise the use of active voice here, there, and everywhere. Simply littering pronouns left and right in UI texts often only results in making the text more linguistically imprecise.

trans-unit.resname: Observability|GitLab Observability is an application monitoring backend included with your project. It's an alternative to Datadog, New Relic, and Dynatrace. Instrument your application with OpenTelemetry to send traces, metrics, and logs, then explore them alongside your commits, pipelines, and issues.
trans-unit.source: Observability|GitLab Observability is an application monitoring backend included with your project. It's an alternative to Datadog, New Relic, and Dynatrace. Instrument your application with OpenTelemetry to send traces, metrics, and logs, then explore them alongside your commits, pipelines, and issues.
trans-unit.target: GitLab Observability är en bakände för applikationsövervakning som ingår i ditt projekt. Det är ett alternativ till Datadog, New Relic och Dynatrace. Instrumentera din applikation med OpenTelemetry för att skicka spårningar, mätvärden och loggar och utforska dem sedan tillsammans med dina commits, pipelines och ärenden.

trans-unit.resname: Observability|GitLab Observability is an open source, OpenTelemetry-native observability platform that unifies logs, metrics, and traces in a single application. Monitor application performance with APM dashboards, visualize distributed traces across microservices, manage centralized logs with powerful querying, and set up intelligent alerts.
trans-unit.source: Observability|GitLab Observability is an open source, OpenTelemetry-native observability platform that unifies logs, metrics, and traces in a single application. Monitor application performance with APM dashboards, visualize distributed traces across microservices, manage centralized logs with powerful querying, and set up intelligent alerts.
trans-unit.target: GitLab Observability är en observationsplattform med öppen källkod och inbyggt stöd för OpenTelemetry som samlar loggar, mätvärden och spårningar i en enda applikation. Övervaka applikationsprestanda med APM-instrumentpaneler, visualisera distribuerade spårningar mellan mikrotjänster, hantera centraliserade loggar med kraftfulla sökfunktioner och konfigurera intelligenta varningar.

trans-unit.resname: OfflineTransferExport|Export your groups to an AWS S3 storage service you control. You can import them to any GitLab instance, even without a network connection between this instance and the destination instance. Each group is exported with all of its subgroups and projects.
trans-unit.source: OfflineTransferExport|Export your groups to an AWS S3 storage service you control. You can import them to any GitLab instance, even without a network connection between this instance and the destination instance. Each group is exported with all of its subgroups and projects.
trans-unit.target: Exportera dina grupper till en AWS S3-lagringstjänst som du själv kontrollerar. Du kan importera dem till valfri GitLab-instans, även utan en nätverksanslutning mellan den här instansen och mål­instansen. Varje grupp exporteras tillsammans med alla sina undergrupper och projekt.

trans-unit.note: What is this word? Why no space?

Thanks for asking. "Orbit" is a GitLab knowledge graph feature that shows connections between GitLab entities as a visual graph. This string is the display label for the work item entity type - a node in that graph. A work item is the unified task/issue concept in GitLab.
The `WorkItem` spelling in the source is a code identifier used as the string key, not a display format constraint. You can and should translate it as two words if your language needs a space. Translate the concept "work item" as your language would naturally express it.
I will also be loggiing a source quality issue with the developer to replace these CamelCase labels with properly spaced English, which will make future strings clearer for everyone.
@grbear - apologies, forgot to tag you in my previous response above.

trans-unit.resname: OutboundRequests|Requests can be made to these IP addresses and domains even when local requests are not allowed. IP ranges such as %{code_start}1:0:0:0:0:0:0:0/124%{code_end} and %{code_start}127.0.0.0/28%{code_end} are supported. Domain wildcards are not supported. trans-unit.note:
@luzhiyuan.deer , could you please update the translation to replace the reference to JihuLab.com, with GitLab.com, as the English source says? Thank you!
Context:
The string is the subject line of an email (as well a banner). The email is to guide users accessing GitLab from China/Macau/Hong Kong to migrate to Jihu. In this case, the current translation incorrectly tells them to migrate from JihuLab instead of GitLab.
Please see more specific details in (1) the original merge requests and (2) at the context URL below the string:
1. https://gitlab.com/gitlab-org/gitlab/-/merge_requests/175147 https://gitlab.com/gitlab-org/gitlab/-/merge_requests/171902
2. https://gitlab-com.gitlab.io/localization/gitlab-string-search/?search=PIPL%7CImportant+Change+to+Your+GitLab%2Ecom+Account
Thank you for the reminder! It has been updated.

trans-unit.resname: PIPL|Please be advised that GitLab can no longer service GitLab.com accounts for individuals and organizations located in Mainland China, Macao, and Hong Kong. Our system indicates that you are visiting GitLab from one of these locations. We advise you to sign up with JiHu %{jihu_link}. JiHu is an independent company with a localized GitLab offering that has an exclusive right to provide GitLab to individuals and organizations located in this region. You must complete the transition by %{deadline}, after which GitLab will delete your account from our systems. If you believe you are receiving this notification in error, please log in to GitLab.com from a supported service location. For further information or support, please feel free to contact %{email}.
trans-unit.source: PIPL|Please be advised that GitLab can no longer service GitLab.com accounts for individuals and organizations located in Mainland China, Macao, and Hong Kong. Our system indicates that you are visiting GitLab from one of these locations. We advise you to sign up with JiHu %{jihu_link}. JiHu is an independent company with a localized GitLab offering that has an exclusive right to provide GitLab to individuals and organizations located in this region. You must complete the transition by %{deadline}, after which GitLab will delete your account from our systems. If you believe you are receiving this notification in error, please log in to GitLab.com from a supported service location. For further information or support, please feel free to contact %{email}.
trans-unit.target: Observera att GitLab inte längre kan tillhandahålla tjänster för GitLab.com-konton som tillhör privatpersoner och organisationer i Fastlandskina, Macao och Hongkong. Vårt system visar att du besöker GitLab från en av dessa platser. Vi rekommenderar att du registrerar dig hos JiHu %{jihu_link}. JiHu är ett oberoende företag med en lokaliserad GitLab-tjänst som har exklusiv rätt att tillhandahålla GitLab till privatpersoner och organisationer i denna region. Du måste slutföra övergången senast %{deadline}, varefter GitLab kommer att radera ditt konto från våra system. Om du anser att du har fått det här meddelandet av misstag kan du logga in på GitLab.com från en plats där tjänsten stöds. För mer information eller support är du välkommen att kontakta %{email}.

trans-unit.resname: PIPL|Please be advised that GitLab can no longer service GitLab.com accounts for individuals and organizations located in Mainland China, Macao, and Hong Kong. JiHu is an independent company with a localized GitLab offering that has exclusive rights to provide GitLab to individuals and organizations located in this region. You have %{deadline} days to complete the transition, after which GitLab will delete your account from our systems. I fixed your wrong translation.

The Portuguese translation of "tab" with the meaning of the "tab character" should be "tabulação" (feminine) or just "tab" (masculine)
The word used, "aba", refers to a flap, and it's commonly used for tab but only in the context of UI (as in a tab of a browser)

@abutkeev , what's your recommendation for the best terminology choice between the following 3 options for the term "squash"? склеивать, сжимать, объединять (and their derivative nouns or verbs in the predictive aspect)
@oleksandr.pysaryuk I think склеивать is the best choise to describe git squash process

@abutkeev , the RU equivalent in the glossary seems to be the English-looking "squash".
Please ignore the glossary for now. We are looking into improving it overall, first with the approach then with content inside: -- https://gitlab.com/gitlab-com/localization/localization-team/-/issues/278 -- https://gitlab.com/gitlab-com/localization/localization-team/-/issues/233
Feel free to start an issue, tag me, and suggest additions to the glossary and their equivalent translations. The process (at least until we improve it) is straightforward: https://docs.gitlab.com/ee/development/i18n/translation.html#updating-the-glossary
"сжатие" sounds good. Thank you. I have recorded the decision in an issue, in case we need to revisit: https://gitlab.com/gitlab-com/localization/localization-team/-/issues/337

trans-unit.resname: Promotions|Webhooks allow you to trigger a URL if, for example, new code is pushed or a new issue is created. You can configure webhooks to listen for specific events like pushes, issues or merge requests. Group webhooks will apply to all projects in a group, allowing you to standardize webhook functionality across your entire group.
trans-unit.source: Promotions|Webhooks allow you to trigger a URL if, for example, new code is pushed or a new issue is created. You can configure webhooks to listen for specific events like pushes, issues or merge requests. Group webhooks will apply to all projects in a group, allowing you to standardize webhook functionality across your entire group.
trans-unit.target: Webhooks gör att du kan utlösa en URL när till exempel ny kod skickas upp eller ett nytt ärende skapas. Du kan konfigurera webhooks så att de lyssnar efter specifika händelser, till exempel uppskickningar, ärenden eller sammanslagningsförfrågningar. Gruppwebhooks gäller för alla projekt i en grupp, vilket gör att du kan standardisera webhook-funktionaliteten i hela gruppen.

trans-unit.note: Brazilian proofreader, please consider reviewing the current translation "Responda a este e-mail diretamente ou%{view_it_on_gitlab}.", as it is missing a space after "ou". This is part of the footnote in GitLab's email notification

The phrase in portuguese “Responda a este e-mail diretamente ou visualizá-lo no GitLab.” is grammatically correct, but it does sound a bit formal and less natural in everyday Portuguese. In particular, “visualizá-lo” feels like a direct translation of “view it on GitLab.” A more natural phrasing would be: “Responda a este e-mail diretamente ou visualize este e-mail no GitLab.”

@grbear & @akairri & @gitlab: Believe this is to be understood as "Copy failed test names to make them run locally (instead)".
Unfortunately, you shouldn't expect GitLab to assist you in any way. Apparently, they like free, voluntary translators very much, yet they don't provide any context info at all, nor do they bother to reply to translator requests, even though these requests are made with the purpose of providing the best localization possible.
What they expect translators to do, however, is to spend even more of your precious spare time going to their site to dig up the info you need on your own (that's why this text "The text is used in gitlab.pot. Position in file: 10709 File: gitlab.pot" is provided in the CONTEXT section!).
What a great way of appreciating the efforts of a free workforce! "They do a lot of work already, let's make them work even more, after all, they're doing it completely free of charge!".

@NCAA thanks for your reply, I'm pretty new here and I expected they provided more context but now I see this is pure free workforce for them. I'll try to contribute whenever I can but I don't think the translations are going to be so accurate if we just have a bare sentence and nothing else.

@nicklcanada
How do you get that now? Firstly, I already know this, secondly, you are writing this to me from the Romanic language, but I am a proofreader for German...

@Justman10000 First of all, I don't write from Romanic but from Romanian language. Secondly, if you know the rule, that's perfect. Don't feel frustrated, I just wanted to help you. I won't bother you again from now on.

@akairri: You're most welcome. :-)
The lack of proper (or, for that matter, any) context info is just a sign of sheer stupidity if you ask me.
When you rely heavily on voluntary resources, such as translators, to get a piece of work done, then the very least you could do is to provide the best conditions for doing the job.
Unfortunately, not providing proper context info is commonly neglected by many projects who use either GitHub or any of the other Git "flavors", as they expect translators to use the links provided in the context section to go to their repos to point out errors, ask questions, etc.
Crowdin provides a platform and environment from where all the work should be performed. Project owners can use a slew of different integrations to integrate their crowdin project with projects and resources elsewhere, and they can have crowdin develop whatever types of integrations, etc. that they need to ensure that all work can be done exclusively on the crowdin platform, yet many still expect translators to spend additional time on external sites in order to be able to perform their work on crowdin.
To me, this is just a completely idiotic strategy, one that will only lead to poorer translation results, i.e., an overall low-quality localization outcome compared to what it could have been, had translators been given adequate info from the start and gotten their questions answered (in a timely fashion).
I'll never be able to understand why project owners, who use this strategy, even use crowdin, when they obviously don't care about what type of localization they will eventually get. You must really not care about your product at all if you expose it to this treatment! Just incomprehensible stupidity.

trans-unit.resname: Runners|A capacity of 1 enables warm HA through Auto Scaling group re-spawn. A capacity of 2 enables hot HA because the service is available even when a node is lost. A capacity of 3 or more enables hot HA and manual scaling of runner fleet.
trans-unit.source: Runners|A capacity of 1 enables warm HA through Auto Scaling group re-spawn. A capacity of 2 enables hot HA because the service is available even when a node is lost. A capacity of 3 or more enables hot HA and manual scaling of runner fleet.
trans-unit.target: En kapacitet på 1 möjliggör varm hög tillgänglighet (HA) genom att Auto Scaling-gruppen återskapar instansen. En kapacitet på 2 möjliggör het hög tillgänglighet eftersom tjänsten förblir tillgänglig även om en nod går förlorad. En kapacitet på 3 eller fler möjliggör het hög tillgänglighet och manuell skalning av runner-flottan.

trans-unit.resname: Runners|Maximum amount of time the runner can run before it terminates. The job timeout of the runner is used if it is shorter than the project job timeout. For example, if the maximum job timeout for a runner is 30 minutes, but the CI/CD timeout for a project is 2 hours, the job running in that project times out after 30 minutes.
trans-unit.source: Runners|Maximum amount of time the runner can run before it terminates. The job timeout of the runner is used if it is shorter than the project job timeout. For example, if the maximum job timeout for a runner is 30 minutes, but the CI/CD timeout for a project is 2 hours, the job running in that project times out after 30 minutes.
trans-unit.target: Den maximala tid som en runner får köras innan den avslutas. Runnerns tidsgräns för jobb används om den är kortare än projektets tidsgräns för jobb. Om den maximala tidsgränsen för ett jobb på en runner till exempel är 30 minuter, men CI/CD-tidsgränsen för ett projekt är 2 timmar, får jobbet som körs i projektet en tidsgräns på 30 minuter.

trans-unit.note: This is not a mistake but no category was appropriate for this issue. In fact, this type of sentence with a variable is problematic in French. Here, when the variable is "Inject" or "Override", we have to translate it into "Injecter/Remplacer", and we have to add "le" before "pipeline file" to make sense. But if we add "le", when applying the variable "Schedule a new", the French version is no longer correct as we get "Planifier un nouveau le fichier de pipeline" which results in something wrong like "schedule a new the pipeline file". The proper solution would be to include the determiner with the verb (i.e "Injecter le") during the translation, but only "Schedule a new" is available in this translation task. Could you add the relevant strings please so that we can translate them properly? Otherwise we might get a final sentence which is not grammatically correct in French.
@oleksandr.pysaryuk could you please report this in order to update the source English? Thanks,

trans-unit.note: There is an inconsistency in the translation of the term "secrets" in the glossary: secret=segredo / secret detection=detecção de senhas. I don't particularly like the term "segredo" in this context, "senhas" makes more sense to me. However, the word "senhas" is also used in PTBR for "passwords". How shall we proceed? Following the glossary, inconsistency included, for now.

@FKP Hi! We believe that the best approach would be suggesting new terms for "secret", "secret detection" and "password" in order to avoid inconsistencies. Could you please suggest new terms for them? And we will be able to update the glossary if needed.

context-group.context: See where this string is used in code: https://gitlab-com.gitlab.io/localization/gitlab-string-search/?search=ScanResultPolicy%7CAllow+specific+types+of+branches+to+bypass+policies+based+on+naming+conventions%2E

trans-unit.note: Is it the policies that are based on naming conventions? Or does this mean that, by setting this option, naming conventions will be considered to allow specific types of branches to bypass policies?

@FerBle Great question.
The second interpretation is correct: By setting this option, naming conventions will be considered to allow specific types of branches to bypass policies.
Specifically, the "Source Branch Patterns" exception type allows you to define naming patterns that let certain branches bypass security policies. In the original MR (https://gitlab.com/gitlab-org/gitlab/-/merge_requests/192723), you can see:
Description: "Allow specific types of branches to bypass policies based on naming conventions."
Example: "If you want to allow all hotfix branches to bypass approval requirements during production incidents, use 'hotfix/*' to match branches like hotfix/payment-bug and hotfix/security-patch."
This feature is part of GitLab's security orchestration system where one can create exceptions to security policies. The branch pattern matching works by:
1. You define a naming pattern (like hotfix/* or feature/*) 2. Any branch matching that pattern can bypass the security policies 3. This is useful for emergency situations or specific workflows that need to skip normal approval processes
The policies themselves are not based on naming conventions - rather, the naming conventions are used as criteria to determine which branches can bypass existing policies.
Hope this helps!
That was indeed very useful, thank you!
@fu7mu4 I adjusted the wording.

trans-unit.note: @sravanelli @victoriaovando just a sugegstion: "Secrets Manager" should be added to glossary, TM is not consistent. Thanks!

@WP_requests Thank you for your flag! In GitLab's context, "secrets manager" is found in two cases: - GitLab Secrets Manager: a specific GitLab-native feature for storing and managing secrets, currently in development/experiment phase. It should DNT. - secrets manager: (usually in lowercase letters) a broader term referring to any secrets management tool or integration.
In light of this, please keep GitLab Secrets Manager as is in the target text as well.
@sravanelli Done! All strings fixed now. Please add it to the termbase as a global choice so it's clear for everybody :)

trans-unit.resname: SecurityConfiguration|Once you've enabled a scan for the default branch, any subsequent feature branch you create will include the scan. An enabled scanner will not be reflected as such until the pipeline has been successfully executed and it has generated valid artifacts.
trans-unit.source: SecurityConfiguration|Once you've enabled a scan for the default branch, any subsequent feature branch you create will include the scan. An enabled scanner will not be reflected as such until the pipeline has been successfully executed and it has generated valid artifacts.
trans-unit.target: När du har aktiverat en skanning för standardgrenen kommer alla efterföljande funktionsgrenar som du skapar att inkludera skanningen. En aktiverad skanner visas dock inte som aktiverad förrän pipelinen har körts framgångsrikt och genererat giltiga artefakter.

trans-unit.note: Need more context. What is "modified"?

@SabrinaDeVellis : the text label "Modified" (SecurityExclusions|Modified) appears as a column header in a table that lists security exclusions. It indicates when a security exclusion rule was last changed or updated.
The column shows the time elapsed since the last modification of an exclusion rule. For example, it might show values like "3 days ago" to indicate when the exclusion was last modified.
Here is more context: https://gitlab.com/gitlab-org/gitlab/-/merge_requests/166464
Cc @Martin005 @victoriaovando
@oleksandr.pysaryuk, thank you very much!

trans-unit.note: Is "trigger" here a verb (as in a button to trigger something) or a noun (as in the action or event that causes something else to trigger)?

@FerBle In GitLab's context, "SecurityOrchestration|Trigger" refers to "Trigger" as a noun. It represents the event or mechanism that initiates a security orchestration workflow or process, not the action of triggering something. This is consistent with GitLab's terminology in security orchestration contexts, where "triggers" are defined conditions or events that cause security workflows to execute automatically. It's similar to how CI/CD pipelines have triggers that initiate them based on certain events.
@oleksandr.pysaryuk Thank you, that was really helpful!

För att interagera med en länk i en popup-ruta i ett diagram klickar du först för att fästa popup-rutan. Klicka utanför popup-rutan för att lossa den. Den här instrumentpanelen kan visa ett högre totalt antal sårbarheter än sårbarhetsrapporten, som delar upp resultaten mellan flikarna Utveckling, Drift och Containerregister. %{learnMoreStart}Läs mer%{learnMoreEnd}

trans-unit.resname: Set the default expiration time for job artifacts in all projects. Set to %{code_open}0%{code_close} to never expire artifacts by default. If no unit is written, it defaults to seconds. For example, these are all equivalent: %{code_open}3600%{code_close}, %{code_open}60 minutes%{code_close}, or %{code_open}one hour%{code_close}.
trans-unit.source: Set the default expiration time for job artifacts in all projects. Set to %{code_open}0%{code_close} to never expire artifacts by default. If no unit is written, it defaults to seconds. For example, these are all equivalent: %{code_open}3600%{code_close}, %{code_open}60 minutes%{code_close}, or %{code_open}one hour%{code_close}.
trans-unit.target: Ange standardtiden för när jobb-artefakter upphör att gälla i alla projekt. Ange %{code_open}0%{code_close} för att artefakter som standard aldrig ska upphöra att gälla. Om ingen enhet anges används sekunder som standard. Följande är till exempel likvärdiga: %{code_open}3600%{code_close}, %{code_open}60 minuter%{code_close} eller %{code_open}en timme%{code_close}.

trans-unit.note:
The currently approved translation is not correct, please review my translation, 1. Syntax error because of "%{code_close}" where a %{code_open} belongs too; 2. Uncommon expression "Wenn keine Einheit geschrieben wird" 3. Value to set is translated but should be set literal (eg. "one hour" instead of "eine Stunde")
"Lege die Standardablaufzeit für Job-Artefakte in allen Projekten fest. Auf %{code_open}0%{code_close} setzen, um Artefakte nie ablaufen zu lassen. Wenn keine Einheit angegeben wird, wird standardmäßig Sekunden verwendet. Diese Angaben sind dann zum Beispiel alle äquivalent: %{code_open}3.600%{code_close}, %{code_open}60 minutes%{code_close} oder %{code_open}one hour%{code_close}."
@gnasus-casus I'm not sure if point 3 really shouldn't be translated. But I approved it for now since the other two points are correct.

trans-unit.note: @veronica.carascosi "Alle Tickets anschauen" can be quiet easily confused and I would flag this as a mistranslation. "Showing all issues" means that all issues are already shown, but "Alle Tickets anschauen" translates to "Show all issues". GitLab wants to show a status (e.g. that everything is loaded) and not an action (e.g. load/show all issues).

trans-unit.source: To remove the %{link_start}read-only%{link_end} state and regain write access, ask your top-level group owner(s) to reduce the number of users in your top-level group to %{free_limit} users or less, or to upgrade to a paid tier which do not have user limits.
trans-unit.target: För att ta bort det %{link_start}skrivskyddade%{link_end} läget och återfå skrivåtkomst ber du ägaren eller ägarna till din grupp på högsta nivån att minska antalet användare i gruppen till %{free_limit} användare eller färre, eller att uppgradera till en betalplan som inte har några användargränser.

trans-unit.resname: To remove the %{link_start}read-only%{link_end} state and regain write access, you can reduce the number of users in your top-level group to %{free_limit} users or less. You can also upgrade to a paid tier, which do not have user limits. If you need additional time, you can start a free %{duration}-day trial which includes unlimited users.
trans-unit.source: To remove the %{link_start}read-only%{link_end} state and regain write access, you can reduce the number of users in your top-level group to %{free_limit} users or less. You can also upgrade to a paid tier, which do not have user limits. If you need additional time, you can start a free %{duration}-day trial which includes unlimited users.
trans-unit.target: För att ta bort det %{link_start}skrivskyddade%{link_end} läget och återfå skrivåtkomst kan du minska antalet användare i din grupp på högsta nivån till %{free_limit} användare eller färre. Du kan också uppgradera till en betalplan, som inte har några användargränser. Om du behöver mer tid kan du starta en kostnadsfri provperiod på %{duration} dagar, som inkluderar obegränsat antal användare.

trans-unit.note: Should this also be translated into my language or do I just add the same word?
It would be nice to have an update about this.

@Umeaboy thank you for your question , and sorry for not responding earlier. Hope this helps: the context URL (https://gitlab-com.gitlab.io/localization/gitlab-string-search/?search=True) takes me to the two original MRs where the string was introduced.
1) The first is a string value of "LDAP sync" filter over Users in Admin area - https://gitlab.com/gitlab-org/gitlab/-/merge_requests/187105.
2) And the second is a part of radio group "True" or "False" - you can see that in https://gitlab.com/gitlab-org/gitlab/-/merge_requests/175791 - the video "After" at 0:16.
Here is documentation that may be related to the first MR: https://docs.gitlab.com/administration/auth/ldap/. They do not directly offer the answer, but they suggest that these boolean values are best left un-translated. They are used in the conext of a filter parameter only.
Here is documentation that's directly related about the 2nd MR: https://docs.gitlab.com/user/application_security/dast/browser/configuration/variables/#authentication. The True and False are boolean values, so it's best to leave them un-translated.
If you leave it un-translated, it will show as un-translated in both contexts 1 and 2 where the string is used, and thats fine. Thanks!

trans-unit.note:
Helpful context:
Question: What does Source mean in this case? a system (code repo, issue tracking) from which something is imported to GitLab?
Answer: Source...means the originating user. This is within the context of imports.... User mapping is the process where when you transfer or import a group to a different GitLab instance, you need to make sure the contributions of , for example user 'Susan' in the old instance are assigned correctly to user 'Susan' in the new instance. Susan in the old instance would be the 'source user'.
Also, please see more visual context in this original merge request: https://gitlab.com/gitlab-org/gitlab/-/merge_requests/164152

context-group.context: See where this string is used in code: https://gitlab-com.gitlab.io/localization/gitlab-string-search/?search=UserProfile%7CEmail+confirmation+code+last+sent+at%3A

trans-unit.note: Please, clarify if it correct to assume that after "sent at:" there will be a time.
The question is: Confirm it is correct to assume that after "sent at:" there will be a time, from URL provided there is 0 content after "at:"

@Proofer_IT , please see the code here: https://gitlab.com/gitlab-org/gitlab/-/blob/master/app/views/admin/users/show.html.haml
You may see that the actual string is followed by this code: @user.locked_at&.to_fs(:medium) || _('never')
After the text "Locked account email verification code last sent at:", the following will appear:
The value of @user.locked_at formatted as a medium-length date/time string if it exists, or The word "never" if @user.locked_at is nil.
In this code, to_fs is a method used for formatting dates and times in Ruby on Rails. It stands for "to format string" or "to formatted string".
Specifically, to_fs(:medium) is used several times in this code to format date/time objects into a human-readable string using a predefined format called :medium.
The :medium format typically produces a string like "Dec 04, 2007 11:01:56"
So the full text could be something like: "Locked account email verification code last sent at: June 15, 2023 14:30 (code expired)" or "Locked account email verification code last sent at: never"
Hope this helps!
@oleksandr.pysaryuk Thanks so much! Indeed, we would never guess that. Thanks!

trans-unit.note:
@luzhiyuan.deer I think Repetition and inaccuracy: “美国国土安全部（美国国土安全部的一部分）” – The first part “美国国土安全部” is wrong because CISA is not the Department of Homeland Security itself. Also repeating “美国国土安全部” is confusing. A better way: "美国网络安全与基础设施安全局，隶属于美国国土安全部"
“维护已知被利用的漏洞（也称为"KEV"）漏洞目录 – This is awkward. “KEV” stands for Known Exploited Vulnerabilities, so writing “漏洞目录” after “已知被利用的漏洞” makes it redundant. Also “漏洞目录” should be attached to the abbreviation clearly.
“这些漏洞已在野外被利用” – “in the wild” in cybersecurity means real-world attacks, not literally “野外”. The common Chinese term is “在野利用” . “已有在野利用的漏洞” is much better and accurate.
Your translation mistakenly translated the quotation marks as " I think it should be translated correctly as "or“

trans-unit.resname: Vulnerability|Code flow helps trace and flag risky data ('tainted data') as it moves through your software. Vulnerabilities are detected by pinpointing how untrusted inputs, like user data or network traffic, are utilized. This technique finds and fixes data handling flaws, securing software from injection and cross-site scripting attacks.
trans-unit.source: Vulnerability|Code flow helps trace and flag risky data ('tainted data') as it moves through your software. Vulnerabilities are detected by pinpointing how untrusted inputs, like user data or network traffic, are utilized. This technique finds and fixes data handling flaws, securing software from injection and cross-site scripting attacks.
trans-unit.target: Kodflöde hjälper till att spåra och flagga riskfyllda data (”förorenade data”) när de rör sig genom din programvara. Sårbarheter upptäcks genom att fastställa hur opålitliga indata, till exempel användardata eller nätverkstrafik, används. Den här tekniken hjälper till att hitta och åtgärda brister i datahanteringen och skyddar programvaran mot injektionsattacker och cross-site scripting-attacker.

trans-unit.note: Could you confirm if this refers to the entry point of a trace (as opposed to tracing an entry point). The images and context information uploaded don't include this string so I couldn't see how it is used in context.

@FerBle
"Trace Entry Point" refers to the entry point of a code trace (i.e., the starting point in a code flow trace), not "tracing an entry point."
Here's the context: In vulnerability code flow analysis, data is traced from a source (where untrusted input enters) through intermediate steps to a sink (where the data is used in a risky way). Each step in this trace is displayed in a UI list with badges labeled "source" or "sink."
However, for unverified vulnerabilities, the scanner detected the vulnerability without identifying the actual untrusted input source. In this case, the badge that would normally say "source" is replaced with "Trace Entry Point" to indicate that this is simply where the code flow trace begins, but it is not a confirmed source of untrusted data.
So the meaning is: "The entry point of the [code flow] trace" - the first step in the traced path through the code. It's a UI label on a badge that replaces the word "source" when the source is unverified. The accompanying popover text confirms this: "Unverified vulnerability does not have a source. This means that the vulnerability was detected without identifying the untrusted input that caused it."
@oleksandr.pysaryuk Thank you! :)

trans-unit.target: När du överför projektet till en grupp kan du enkelt hantera flera projekt, visa användningskvoter för lagring, beräkningsminuter och användare samt starta en provperiod eller uppgradera till en betald nivå.
