trans-unit.resname: When your trial ends, you'll move to the Free tier. Free top-level namespaces with private visibility can have only %{free_user_limit} users. If your namespace exceeds this limit, it will become %{read_only_start}read-only%{read_only_end}. To prevent this, %{upgrade_start}upgrade to a paid tier%{upgrade_end}.
trans-unit.source: When your trial ends, you'll move to the Free tier. Free top-level namespaces with private visibility can have only %{free_user_limit} users. If your namespace exceeds this limit, it will become %{read_only_start}read-only%{read_only_end}. To prevent this, %{upgrade_start}upgrade to a paid tier%{upgrade_end}.
trans-unit.target: När provperioden är slut går du över till gratisnivån. Kostnadsfria namnrymder på högsta nivån med privat synlighet kan endast ha %{free_user_limit} användare. Om din namnrymd överskrider den här gränsen blir den %{read_only_start}skrivskyddad%{read_only_end}. För att förhindra detta kan du %{upgrade_start}uppgradera till en betalplan%{upgrade_end}.

trans-unit.note: After long deep searches (by going back to the original blames as requested in the search procedure), I was not able to find the context needed for this string. Could you please add a screenshot?

@SabrinaDeVellis , thank you for doing deep reseacrh! The original merge request contains a screenshot, but I realize it is not showing this exact string, i.e. "Use on": https://gitlab.com/gitlab-org/gitlab/-/merge_requests/179912
Here are some hopefully helpful details:
1. In GitLab, a user would go to a group's settings page 2. Navigate to "Work items" → "Custom fields" section. (Hope you can see some design screenshots linked in this issue: https://gitlab.com/gitlab-org/gitlab/-/issues/500084) 3. Click "Add custom field" or edit an existing custom field
A form will appear with several fields. One of these fields will have the label "Use on" with a dropdown menu below it. This dropdown allows administrators to select which work item types (Issue, Incident, Task, etc.) this custom field should appear on.
For example, if they select "Issue" and "Task" from this dropdown, then the custom field they are creating will only appear when users are viewing or editing Issues and Tasks, but not when they are working with Incidents or other work item types.
I think one of the translation approaches could be to think of "Use on" as a text that conveys the meaning of "apply this custom field to the following work item types."
@oleksandr.pysaryuk thank you very much for your explanation!

이와 동일한 다른 번역들도 전면 수정해야 합니다.

trans-unit.resname: You must have developer or higher permissions in the associated project to view job logs when debug trace is enabled. To disable debug trace, set the 'CI_DEBUG_TRACE' and 'CI_DEBUG_SERVICES' variables to 'false' in your pipeline configuration or CI/CD settings. If you must view this job log, a project maintainer or owner must add you to the project with developer permissions or higher.
trans-unit.source: You must have developer or higher permissions in the associated project to view job logs when debug trace is enabled. To disable debug trace, set the 'CI_DEBUG_TRACE' and 'CI_DEBUG_SERVICES' variables to 'false' in your pipeline configuration or CI/CD settings. If you must view this job log, a project maintainer or owner must add you to the project with developer permissions or higher.
trans-unit.target: Du måste ha Developer-behörighet eller högre i det associerade projektet för att kunna visa jobbloggar när felsökningsspårning är aktiverad. För att inaktivera felsökningsspårning ställer du in variablerna CI_DEBUG_TRACE och CI_DEBUG_SERVICES på false i pipelinekonfigurationen eller CI/CD-inställningarna. Om du måste visa den här jobbloggen behöver en projektansvarig eller ägare lägga till dig i projektet med Developer-behörighet eller högre.

trans-unit.note:
Chain of Custody report The Chain of Custody report allows customers to export a list of merge commits within the group. The data provides a comprehensive view with respect to merge commits. It includes the merge commit SHA, merge request author, merge request ID, merge user, date merged, pipeline ID, group name, project name, and merge request approvers. Depending on the merge strategy, the merge commit SHA can be a merge commit, squash commit, or a diff head commit.
https://docs.gitlab.com/ee/user/compliance/compliance_report/#chain-of-custody-report

trans-unit.note: Is it possible to merge review requests ?
Same as above

@FKP , Great question! I see how the phrase "Your review requests..." may be genuinely confusing if one takes it literally.
Review requests (the things you assign to people) don't get "merged" - rather, merge requests get merged.
The dashboard actually shows merged MRs from two different perspectives:
- "Your merge requests merged in the last 2 weeks" - MRs you authored or are assigned to - "Your review requests merged in the last 2 weeks" - MRs where you were requested as a reviewer
In both cases, it's the merge request that was merged, not the review request. The second message is showing MRs that needed your review and have since been merged.
A bit more detail on how to think about it:
What's actually happening here is - brevity with some technical imprecision, but which becomes clear to a user using GitLab. The full, literal phrasing would be: "Merge requests where you were requested to review, which have now been merged". The shortcut / briefer version just says: "Your review requests merged..." , which is faster to say/read, but technically conflates "review requests" (the assignment) with "merge requests" (the thing being merged).
To sum up: if brevity is not possible to achieve in your target language, a more literal translation option might be: "Merge requests where you were requested to review, merged in the last 2 weeks."
Reference MR: https://gitlab.com/gitlab-org/gitlab/-/merge_requests/220041 Reference docs: https://docs.gitlab.com/tutorials/merge_requests/homepage/

trans-unit.note: Used in Reports|%{no} changed test results
@abutkeev Hi, is this "no" as in denying something? (the opposite of "yes"?) Or is it something else? (short for "number" for instance)

Hi, @FerBle!
In this context, the %{no} variable is used in the string “Reports|%{no} changed test results is not localized.” The possible values are either “no” or a formatted version of “no” (with %{strong_start}no%{strong_end}), both indicating that the test results have not changed.
So, it’s not simply a negation (“no” as the opposite of “yes”) or short for “number,” but rather a dynamic value indicating no changes in the test results. For more details, you can check the merge request here: https://gitlab.com/gitlab-org/gitlab/-/merge_requests/177806.

Thank you @abutkeev for your reply. I did check the merge request before adding my query, but I can't quite figure out how the variable will appear in context. My question is from a linguistic point of view, I'm trying to determine whether this term should be localized into Spanish or just be left as is? If it means "no" as in "no changes", then it's the same in English and Spanish, but if it has some other meaning, then a change might be needed.

Hi @FerBle,
Thanks for the clarification! The %{no} variable in this context is used to indicate "no changes" in the test results. This is currently its only usage, so it doesn't have any other meanings in this context.
Let me know if you have any further questions or need more information!
Thanks @abutkeev! That's exactly what I needed to know :) Thank you so much for the patience :)

trans-unit.note: Hi! Can you please explain the meaning of "target" in this segment? Is it a verb (as in "select all branches"), a complement ("all default branches in target") or neither?

Hi ! Here is the context : https://gitlab.com/-/project/278964/uploads/de37dc1740603eed29c7d5b7c99ca2d1/Screenshot_2025-05-12_at_15.27.29.png but the meaning remains unclear because "triggers every time a pipeline runs for target all protected branches" can mean "...runs in order to target all protected branches" or "... runs for all protected target branches". In both cases, English seems problematic... Doesn't it? @oleksandr.pysaryuk

@SabrinaDeVellis @FKP The correct interpretation is "triggers every time a pipeline runs for branches that are protected." In this context, "target all protected branches" is a selection option where "target" is a verb meaning "to select" or "to apply to." A clearer way to phrase this in documentation or UI would be:
"triggers every time a pipeline runs on any protected branch" "triggers every time a pipeline runs for any of the protected branches"
The current phrasing is technically grammatically awkward in English too. It's combining the UI option label ("target all protected branches") directly into a sentence without adapting it, which creates the confusion you have identified.
Hope this helps translate the string as it is.
Let me see what can be done to improve the source

@oleksandr.pysaryuk Thank you for the explanation. For a better understanding in the English version, the whole sentence would ideally be resegmented this way (deleting "for" in the first part of the sentence and adding it or "to" in relevant options): triggers every time a pipeline runs / to target all default branches OR for all branches. For your information, in the French version, the different options are not problematic because we use "pour" in all cases.
@SabrinaDeVellis and @oleksandr.pysaryuk, thank you both for your input. I get it now. PTBR translation has been fixed.

@oleksandr.pysaryuk Could you confirm that this means "from source branch to target branch" please?

@SabrinaDeVellis @JeukHwang , based on the merge request content at the context URL https://gitlab-com.gitlab.io/localization/gitlab-string-search/?search=to , I can confirm that the msgid "to" in this context does indeed mean "from source branch to target branch."
This "to" appears between two input fields for source and target branches, creating a directional flow that should be translated as a preposition indicating "from source branch to target branch" rather than other meanings of "to."
The larger context is, this is part of GitLab's security policy management feature where users can define branch patterns that bypass policy requirements, and the "to" helps users understand the relationship between source and target branches in their pattern definitions.
I realize that the string "to" is quite ambiguous for translators when taken in isolation. Let me see what we can do to improve the UX in general.
@oleksandr.pysaryuk thank you!
